title: Machine chats that keep up, and tell you when they need you
items: Machines: chats now keep their permission mode, so a chat stays as careful (or as hands-off) as you set it.
Machines: replies from Claude on your machines appear live as they are written, instead of all at once at the end.
Machines: notifications when Claude needs your OK or finishes a task. Tapping one opens that exact chat. Turn them off in Settings > Notifications > Claude on your machines.
Nothing is lost when your computer sleeps or changes Wi-Fi: what it said while the connection was dropping is sent again.
Autonomous mode is safer: it still works on its own, but now stops and asks before risky commands, such as ones that delete files, change system settings or overwrite shared code.
Updated legal policies (10 October 2026), and a list of the open-source licences the app uses.
A new app icon.

title: Notifications that work, and checks that never sleep
items: Notifications now reach your phone. The previous build was made without the part that receives them, so nothing arrived. The app also asks once whether it may notify you; you can change that any time in Settings > Notifications.

Two kinds of automation. Always checking: built in and on for everything you connect, Escanor looks every couple of minutes for a failed deployment, a new incident, a tool that stopped syncing or a drop in health, and tells you straight away. Turn on "Also look into it and fix what is safe" on any check and it starts working on the problem too. Set by you: the automations you create, as before.
A new Automatic checks switch in Settings > Notifications, and a notification about an automation or a check opens the Automations tab.
This release is signed with Escanor's release key. If you installed a test build of 1.24 or 1.25, uninstall it once before installing this one.

title: Escanor works on its own
items: Chats on your machines now work on their own by default. Escanor answers its own permission prompts, checks the logs and results itself, fixes what failed and goes round again until the work is done. It only stops for the few things that cannot be undone, such as wiping a disk or force-pushing over a main branch.

New Automations tab: give Escanor a goal, or set an automation that starts it with nobody asking (every morning, when a deployment fails, when an incident opens, when health drops). See every run, what it decided and why, answer the rare question it needs from you, and stop everything with one tap.
Machines and Computers are now one tab with a Servers and Computers switch, instead of two tabs that looked alike.

Escanor AI and the chats on your servers and computers now look and work the same: your words in a bubble, answers with highlighted code, one line that shows what it is doing and for how long, and a question that needs you pinned above the message box with Continue or Don’t do this.
Pick the model Escanor AI answers with (Auto, or one you choose) and see which of your services it can work on, right under the message box.

Search finds chats by what was said in them, not only by their names, with the sentence that matched under each one. Escanor AI search also understands meaning, so “money spent on cloud” finds the chat about your AWS bill.
Each chat on a machine now keeps its mode, model and effort, so Autonomous no longer resets when you leave and come back.
Your messages show the moment you send them, Stop stops right away, and an answer to a permission prompt no longer waits 30 seconds when the connection is stuck.
Chats refresh every time you open them, and a connection that silently died is replaced, so nothing sits frozen until you go back and in again.
Settings for every chat and every machine: details, rename, defaults for new chats, delete or remove.

Everything now reads inside the app. The links that opened the website are gone: the setup guide, About, the legal documents and their cross-links all open here. This What's new page appears after every update.

title: The new Escanor app
items: The Escanor app is now built with Flutter and replaces the earlier web-based app. It installs next to the old one, so you sign in again and can then remove the old app.
Machines: chats keep their mode and settings, messages and Stop respond at once, and chats refresh when you open them.
Settings sheets for each chat and each machine.
